papers.title: How Do Large Language Monkeys Get Their Power (Laws)?
papers.summary: Explains why repeated LLM sampling yields aggregate power-law scaling even though each individual problem scales exponentially, via heavy-tailed difficulty distributions.

papers.title: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
papers.summary: Adaptively allocating extra computation at inference time, matched to problem difficulty, can outperform a 14× larger pretrained model on easy-to-medium tasks.

papers.title: An Architecture Search Framework for Inference-Time Techniques
papers.summary: ARCHON automatically searches for optimal combinations of inference-time techniques (ensembling, fusion, ranking, critiquing) across multiple LLMs to outperform frontier models by 15.1% on average.

papers.title: Large Language Monkeys: Scaling Inference Compute with Repeated Sampling
papers.summary: Sampling a model thousands of times per problem keeps raising the fraction of problems solved by at least one attempt — but only pays off where a verifier can find the right attempt.
